correctness.rationale: For the lift \(T(\theta)=\theta+\omega-s\sin(\theta+\gamma)\), the exact derivative \(T\prime(\theta)=1-s\cos(\theta+\gamma)\) yields a real-analytic diffeomorphism for \(|s|<1\), one cubic critical point at \(|s|=1\) with \(T\prime\prime\prime=1\), and two folds for \(|s|>1\) with \(|T\prime\prime|=\sqrt{s^2-1}\). Möbius conjugation of Poisson measures and rigidity of orientation-preserving Haar-preserving circle homeomorphisms proves all-strength Poisson nonclosure in the diffeomorphic range. A nonrotation boundary Möbius derivative has a nonzero second Fourier harmonic, whereas \(1-s\cos(\theta+\gamma)\) does not. Positive transfer-density branch sums and Taylor inversion give the exact critical coefficient \(2P_a(c)/6^{2/3}\) and fold coefficient \(P_a(c)\sqrt{2/|T\prime\prime(c)|}\), including coincident folds. Integrability of these positive power singularities proves strict \(L^p\) cutoffs \(3/2\) and \(2\), including divergence at equality. The standard-library numerical checks corroborate, but do not replace, the analytic argument.

originality.rationale: The 2026 preprint explicitly reports qualitative numerical failure of Ott–Antonsen closure. A published record gives a weak-amplitude quadratic circular-cumulant cascade for exactly the same kick. Both facts are excluded from the novelty claim. The proposed theorem is stronger in amplitude and different in observable: it proves exact Poisson nonclosure at every nonzero kick and fully classifies density boundedness and sharp endpoint \(L^p\) thresholds at/above the fold threshold. The published 2023 circle-map analysis supplies the known injectivity boundary but not pushforward Poisson-density coefficients or \(L^p\) thresholds. The 2020 Möbius-map construction is a distinct exact closure-preserving evolution. No full-text covering result was identified in inspected accessible works; incomplete access to the source preprint and broad classical singularity theory remain priority risks.

value.rationale: The 2026 continuum discrete-oscillator preprint motivates understanding how a Poisson/Ott-Antonsen phase density behaves under the actual nonlinear transfer map. A complete nonperturbative closure criterion and sharp loss of density regularity at an explicitly observable effective coupling give more information than known weak-coupling moment failure or the classical map invertibility threshold. The two different, exact \(L^p\) critical values are natural regularity invariants affecting how phase-density transfer is represented and approximated. The result is bounded to one step and does not purport to solve long-time collective synchronization.
